heading: Temporal
text:
### Temporal [LSER.16.9]

| Function | Meaning | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `first(cursor)` | value of first (oldest) sample | slot type, nullable |
| `last(cursor)` | value of last (newest) sample | slot type, nullable |
| `rate(cursor)` | `(last - first) / elapsed_seconds` | `Float?` |
| `direction(cursor)` | `-1` falling, `0` steady or `+1` rising, the sign of the two newest samples' difference ([LSER.10.9]) | `Int?` |

Each is `null` exactly when the read is cold ([LSER.19.8]); `direction` is
also `null` when the window holds one sample ([LSER.10.9]), and `rate` is also
`null` when no time elapses between the window's first and last samples — a
window of one sample included — since there is no elapsed time to divide by.

**`rate` is computed in one order.** $x_f$ and $x_l$ are the window's first and
last samples as `Float`, an `Int` sample converting round-to-nearest-even
([LSER.16.3.3]). $t_f$ and $t_l$ are the monotonic instants, in nanoseconds, at
which the engine absorbed them ([LTIM.2.8.2]); on `all_time` the first sample is
the first the instance absorbed. `rate` is

$\frac{(x_l - x_f) \cdot 10^9}{t_l - t_f}$

and the engine **must** evaluate it as correctly rounded IEEE-754 binary64
operations in exactly this order: the subtraction $x_l - x_f$, the
multiplication by $10^9$, and the division by $t_l - t_f$, the exact `Int`
difference converted round-to-nearest-even. A window whose first and last
samples are the same infinity reads NaN, which no slot admits ([LEXP.4.2]).
